'''Maxim Healthcare Services''' is a privately held [[home care|home health]] provider headquartered in [[Columbia, Maryland]]. It is one of two companies formed in 2022 when '''Maxim Healthcare Group''' was split.<ref>{{cite web |title=Maxim Healthcare Group Separates to Form Two Companies |url=https://behavioral.maximhealthcare.com/newsroom/maxim-healthcare-group-separates-to-form-two-companies/ |website=Maxim Healthcare |access-date=3 December 2025 |date=16 February 2022}}</ref> The other company is now known as '''[[Amergis]]''' and is a [[medical outsourcing|medical staffing]] company.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Baines |first1=Kayla |title=Maxim Healthcare Staffing is Now Amergis |url=https://www.amergis.com/resources/maxim-healthcare-staffing-is-now-amergis/ |website=Amergis |access-date=3 December 2025 |date=7 April 2024}}</ref> Maxim was founded in 1988 as MEDCALL Medical Staffing.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20090804104933/http://investing.businessweek.com/research/stocks/private/snapshot.asp?privcapId=4213003 Bloomberg Businessweek]</ref>

== History ==
Maxim Healthcare was founded in 1988.<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 March 2022 |title=Maxim Healthcare Group retires umbrella brand, divisions form two separate companies |url=https://www.staffingindustry.com/Editorial/Healthcare-Staffing-Report/March-10-2022/Maxim-Healthcare-Group-retires-umbrella-brand-divisions-form-two-separate-companies |access-date=21 October 2024 |website=SIA}}</ref>

In 2008, Maxim Healthcare received ACHC Accreditation.{{Needs citation|date=October 2024}}

In June 2020, Maxim Healthcare Services changed their name to ''Maxim Healthcare Group''.{{Needs citation|date=October 2024}}

In February 2022, the company announced it was retiring the Healthcare Group brand, separating into two independent business units - Maxim Healthcare Services and Maxim Healthcare Staffing.<ref>{{Cite web |date=22 February 2022 |title=Maxim Healthcare Group separates to form two companies |url=https://bizmonthly.com/news/business/2022/02/maxim-healthcare-group-separates-to-form-two-companies/ |access-date=19 November 2024 |website=Business Monthly}}</ref>

Maxim Healthcare Staffing rebranded as Amergis in April 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2024-04-23 |title=Fourth-largest healthcare staffing firm rebrands to Amergis |url=https://www.spotlightdata.co/fourth-largest-healthcare-staffing-firm-rebrands-to-amergis-68980/ |access-date=2024-10-21 |website=Spotlight Data |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Litigation ==
Starting in 2009, Maxim and some of its employees came under government scrutiny for alleged fraudulent billings and false statements to health officials, which were “a common practice at Maxim from 2003 through 2009,” according to the U.S. Attorney's office in New Jersey.<ref name="NYT">[http://prescriptions.blogs.nytimes.com/2011/09/12/maxim-healthcare-pays-150-million-in-fraud-case/ "Maxim Healthcare Pays $150 Million in Fraud Case"], New York Times, September 12, 2011.</ref> Between 2009 and 2011, nine current and former Maxim employees including three senior managers pleaded guilty to felony charges.<ref name="NYT" /> In 2011, Maxim entered into agreements with the [[United States Department of Justice]] and affected states to pay $150 million to resolve criminal and civil charges that the company submitted claims for millions of dollars of work that it did not perform and operated offices that were not properly licensed.<ref>[https://www.baltimoresun.com/2011/09/12/columbia-firm-settles-150m-fraud-case-with-federal-government/ "Columbia firm settles $150M fraud case with federal government"] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250125002113/https://www.baltimoresun.com/2011/09/12/columbia-firm-settles-150m-fraud-case-with-federal-government/ |date=2025-01-25 |url-access=subscription}}, Baltimore Sun, September 12, 2011</ref> The Company entered into a Deferred Prosecution Agreement with the United States Attorney's Office for the District of New Jersey, a [[corporate integrity agreement]] with the [[Office of inspector general (United States)|Office of the Inspector General]], U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, and civil settlement agreements with the United States of America and 43 states.<ref>[https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/2011/September/11-civ-1169.html Maxim Healthcare Services Charged with Fraud, Agrees to Pay Approximately $150 Million, Enact Reforms After False Billings Revealed as Common Practice]</ref>
